text:
tara: Alert — saw a spike in keystore audit export QPS in eu-west after retention tweak. privatelink NAT conntrack is hitting limits and several GPU warm-pool nodes are stuck in onboarding.

sre-bot: [ALERT] privatelink-euw conntrack_full x87 in 12m; keystore-exporter 502/504 surge; warmpool-onboard-fail=19.

isaac: Can you paste a node log? need to confirm conntrack vs exporter latency.

tara: node-7 tail: 
```
2026-03-30T22:11:17 kubelet[1234]: Pod warmup failed: GET /keystore meta timeout
kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
keystore-exporter euw latency=1234ms status=504
```

diana: Short mitigations: 1) traffic-shape exporter ingress with Envoy rate limit on privatelink (token-bucket), 2) temporary nf_conntrack_max bump on nat-euw, 3) scoped rollback for exporter-facing retention index to 30-60d if Security approves.

isaac: Envoy rate-limit sounds low-risk. Can we route just the audit-export path through the limiter? We should avoid touching keystore read/write paths used by customers.

tara: yes, we can target exporter path (/export/audit) and keystore service account only. will prepare envoy config.

sre-bot: [INFO] preliminary metric: exporter 95th latency up 4x; conntrack_count=198420 nf_conntrack_max=200000.

diana: Commands for NAT bump if needed: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000` and monitor `/proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count`. Bumping gives breathing room but we need long-term smoothing.

security: retention policy was increased for regulatory reasons. rollbacks need an approval ticket with re-audit plan. Security prefers infra smoothing over retention reductions.

isaac: OK plan: (A) deploy Envoy token-bucket limiter on exporter path (rate=250rps burst=500) as a canary to 10% of privatelink pods, (B) if errors persist bump conntrack_max on NATs for 4h, (C) open COMPL ticket for scoped rollback if needed, include cost delta.

tara: I'll push the envoy config now to 10% canary and watch. starting canary. :eye: 

sre-bot: [METRIC] 5m after canary: exporter 504s down ~50%, conntrack growth slowed; warm-pool join success improved from 24% -> 72%.

diana: Good signal. Keep canary running 20m. If steady, scale to 100% limiter and schedule exporter batching work for next sprint.

security: We approve the canary limiter and a short conntrack bump if strictly needed. No retention rollback without COMPL ticket and re-audit plan.

isaac: Noted. tara, if limiter holds we'll avoid rollback and create a PLAT task for batching+async export. Also capture cost impact for the audit team.

tara: Canary steady at 25m: exporter errors low, warm-pool joins at 88%. I'm scaling limiter to 100% now.

sre-bot: [RESOLVE] alert suppressed. follow-ups: PLAT-13123 exporter-batching, OPS-13124 conntrack-runbook, COMPL-6621 retention-audit-justification.

diana: Action items assigned: (tara) post canary logs to COMPL-6621 and include cost delta; (isaac) schedule batching PoC; (sre) add pre-change conntrack checklist for big auth/retention changes.

isaac: Also propose we add a preflight that simulates exporter reindex QPS on staging NATs to validate conntrack sizing and limiter configs before rolling retention changes.

tara: Agreed. creating a short runbook PR for retention/keystore changes that includes staging spike test, envoy limiter template, and emergency NAT bump steps.

security: Reminder: any temporary exemption must be retracted and re-audited within 48h. attach logs to COMPL-6621.

isaac: Thanks team. closing unless regressions — spawn incidents/ if we need paging.
